description: Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.

c.request: Looking at what has actually been rented (each rental traced through its inventory copy to the film, skipping any that don't link up), what share of the rented films does each film `rating` account for, out of the total across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, give one row with: their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share. No rounding. Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.
c.sql: WITH rated AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rentals FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, rentals, rentals / (SELECT SUM(rentals) FROM rated) AS share FROM rated), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.rentals) AS combined_rentals, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share) - (SELECT a FROM avg_share) AS avg_share_above FROM shares s WHERE s.share > (SELECT a FROM avg_share)

a.request: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the rental transactions, so a film rented many times counts each time. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, cnt, CAST(cnt AS DOUBLE) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM rating_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rating_count, AVG(k.share) AS avg_share, AVG(k.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM kept k CROSS JOIN avg_share a

b.request: Using rental transactions per rating (rental → inventory → film, inner-joined so unlinked rentals drop out), share = rating's rental count ÷ total rental count, and for ratings whose share exceeds the mean of the rating shares, return one row: summed rental count, mean share, and mean of (share − mean share), unrounded
b.sql: WITH rating_counts AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rentals FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, rentals, CAST(rentals AS DOUBLE) / SUM(rentals) OVER () AS share FROM rating_counts), stats AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS mean_share FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.rentals, s.share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN stats st WHERE s.share > st.mean_share) SELECT SUM(a.rentals) AS total_rentals, AVG(a.share) AS mean_share, AVG(a.share - st.mean_share) AS mean_share_deviation FROM above a CROSS JOIN stats st

d.request:
Rewritten as a standalone question:

For the rented films, grouped by their `rating`, what is each rating's share of all rental transactions? Count each rental by tracing it through its inventory copy to the film, and skip any rental that doesn't link to a film. Then, for every rating whose share is above the average share across ratings, return one row with: the combined number of rented films for those ratings, their average share, and how far on average their share exceeds that average share. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH rental_by_rating AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rentals FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, rentals, CAST(rentals AS DOUBLE) / SUM(rentals) OVER () AS share FROM rental_by_rating), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.rentals) AS rented_films, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;
